question.text: What first round vote share will José Maria Neves win in the 2026 Cape Verdean presidential election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage vote share received by José Maria Neves in the first round of the Cape Verdean presidential election scheduled to be held on November 15, 2026, as declared by the [Cape Verdean National Electoral Commission](https://cne.cv/resultados-oficiais/) (CNE) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
question.fine_print:

research:
I'm writing up the findings now. I checked the CNE portal, Wikipedia, local Cape Verdean outlets and the Rio Times explainer.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-25: The CNE presidential portal shows the election date (Sunday 15 November 2026, polls open 08:00-18:00) and has "Candidatos" and "Resultados" sections, but it shows no results or vote totals yet. [presidenciais2026.cne.cv](https://presidenciais2026.cne.cv/)
- To win in the first round a candidate needs more than 50% of valid votes, and blank votes are not counted. If nobody gets there, the top two meet in a runoff on 29 November. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/cabo-verde-presidential-election-us-visitors-2026/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Voting has not happened, and I found no independent polls.
- 2026-09-14: Neves announced he would run for a second term and suspended his mandate. Speaker Janira Hopffer Almada became interim president. [A Nação](https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/09/14/presidenciais-2026-jose-maria-neves-confirma-candidatura-a-segundo-mandato/), [Observador](https://observador.pt/2026/09/14/jose-maria-neves-anuncia-recandidatura-a-presidente-de-cabo-verde/)
- 2026-09-15: The PAICV declared its support for Neves. [A Nação](https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/09/15/presidenciais-2026-paicv-declara-apoio-a-jose-maria-neves/)
- 2026-09-23: The Constitutional Court validated five candidates: Neves (PAICV), Joana Rosa (MpD-backed, former Justice Minister), Gilson Alves, Casimiro Pina and Antero Tavares.
  - Péricles Tavares withdrew. Five applicants were rejected, including Amadeu Oliveira (he is in prison) and Fernando Rocha Delgado (not enough signatures). Delgado urged voters to abstain. [Africas](https://www.africas.com.br/noticia/cabo-verde-define-cinco-candidatos-validados-para-as-eleicoes-presidenciais)
  - Sources disagree on the count: Rio Times lists six on the ballot, adding Loisito Tavares de Sousa (independent), possibly admitted on appeal. I could not confirm which is right. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/cabo-verde-presidential-election-us-visitors-2026/)
- I could not find whether the UCID (5.2% in May) has backed any candidate.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-25: Rio Times says no independent poll has been published. Publishing polls is banned from 29 October until polls close. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/cabo-verde-presidential-election-us-visitors-2026/)
- 2026-10-12: Neves presented five commitments under the slogan "Cabo Verde, Vencer Juntos". [Expresso das Ilhas](https://expressodasilhas.cv/politica/2026/10/12/presidenciais-2026-jose-maria-neves-apresenta-cinco-compromissos-para-mandato/105054)
- 2026-10-01: Rosa, the first woman to run for president, asked to be judged on competence. She has a ten-point manifesto. [Observador](https://observador.pt/2026/10/01/joana-rosa-quer-ser-avaliada-pela-competencia-e-nao-so-por-ser-a-primeira-mulher-candidata-a-presidencia-em-cabo-verde/), [Balai](https://www.balai.cv/noticias/atualidade/presidenciais-2026-joana-rosa-apresenta-dez-compromissos-centrados-na-democracia-juventude-e-coesao-nacional/)
- 2026-07-27: The MpD used an internal poll to choose its candidate from four names. This was about candidate selection, not a measure of voter intention. [A Nação](https://www.anacao.cv/noticia/2026/07/27/presidenciais-de-novembro-de-2026-mpd-recorre-a-sondagem-para-escolher-candidato-e-travar-divisoes-internas/)
- The official campaign reportedly starts 29 October. Only one source says this. [Vida Mundial](https://www.vidamundial.com.pt/eleicoes-presidenciais-em-cabo-verde/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2021: Neves won in the first round with about 51.7-51.8% (Rio Times gives 51.79%). Carlos Veiga (MpD) got about 42%. The minor candidates in that race included Casimiro de Pina (1.80%) and Gilson Alves (0.76%). Neves was then the opposition-backed candidate under an MpD government. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Cape_Verdean_presidential_election), [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/cabo-verde-presidential-election-us-visitors-2026/)
- 2026-05-17 parliamentary election: PAICV 48.04% (90,660 votes), MpD 44.75% (84,458), UCID 5.20%. Turnout was 46.46%, a record low. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Cape_Verdean_parliamentary_election), [Inforpress](https://www.inforpress.cv/en/article-10068)
- 2016: Incumbent Jorge Carlos Fonseca was re-elected in the first round with 74%, with no strong PAICV candidate against him. [RTP](https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/mundo/cabo-verde-jose-maria-neves-espera-eleicao-a-primeira-volta_n1351571)
- Earlier races, from my own memory and not checked here: 2006, incumbent Pires won about 51% against Veiga; 2011, there was a runoff, with Fonseca on about 38% in round one.
- Pattern: Cape Verde politics is closely split between two parties (about 48 vs 45 in May). Presidential first-round shares for the PAICV side have stayed in a narrow band of about 50-52%. This time Neves runs as an incumbent whose party also holds the government, so the cohabitation of his first term has ended.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi (2026-10-25), winning party: PAICV 85%, MpD 15%, UCID 3%. Kalshi, "anyone wins outright on Nov 15": 71%.
- Polymarket (2026-10-25), outright first-round win: 59%. On the winner market, Rosa is at 4.15%. Neves's line was not in the data I was given, but Rio Times reports him at 83%. The contract also lists names not on the ballot, such as Janine Lélis.
- Liquidity is thin on both: about US$34k traded on Polymarket and about 4,200 contracts on Kalshi. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/cabo-verde-presidential-election-us-visitors-2026/)
- If the outright-win probabilities above (59-71%) are read as P(Neves above 50%), they put the market's median slightly above 50%.
- I found no expert or model forecast of vote shares, and no Manifold market.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-10-29 to 2026-11-13: official campaign period, with the poll publication ban starting 29 October.
- 2026-11-15: first round. Preliminary results should come out that night or the next day, followed by the official CNE count.
- 2026-11-29: runoff if needed. It does not affect this question, which is about the first-round share only.
- Factors that could move the outcome:
  - turnout, which hit a record low in May
  - diaspora voting
  - whether the UCID makes an endorsement
  - whether Rosa gets the MpD's full vote of about 45%
  - how much the minor candidates take

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: the first round is on 15 November 2026, about 3 weeks away. Preliminary results should appear that night or the next day, and official CNE results come later in November.

(b) Latest known value: there is no 2026 result yet. The CNE portal showed no results as of 2026-10-25. The relevant reference points are Neves's 2021 first-round share of about 51.8%, and the PAICV's 48.0% in the May 2026 parliamentary election.

(c) If nothing changed: Neves would get roughly his 2021 share, about 51 to 53%. This assumes a two-bloc split like May (PAICV 48 vs MpD 45). Minor candidates would take about 3 to 6%, and Neves would gain a small incumbency premium.

(d) If the current trend continued: the PAICV won government in May, and Neves is a sitting president seeking re-election. In Cape Verde, incumbent presidents have won re-election (Pires in 2006, Fonseca in 2016). A demoralized MpD after its defeat could push Neves into the mid-50s.

(e) Historical variation: PAICV-side presidential first-round shares have been in a narrow band of about 49 to 52% in competitive races. The national swing between elections is typically a few points. In 2016, the main opposition did not field a strong candidate, and the incumbent got 74%. That is not the case now, because the MpD backs Joana Rosa.

(f) Markets: Kalshi gives 71% that someone wins outright, and Polymarket gives 59%. Neves's chance of winning overall is about 83 to 85%. If P(Neves above 50%) is about 60 to 65%, the implied median is roughly 52 to 53%. There are no polls, and poll publication is banned from 29 October.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low outcome: Rosa consolidates the full MpD vote plus UCID voters, minor candidates draw protest votes, and low PAICV turnout pushes Neves to around 43 to 46%, forcing a runoff.
- High outcome: the MpD is demoralized after its May defeat and Rosa underperforms. The incumbency effect and a weak field (like 2016) then give Neves around 60% or more.
